resources.title: SNES360 Enhanced
resources.author: frankischilling · Snes9x / original Snes360 contributors
resources.description: Standalone Snes9x 1.51 port with ROM search, favorites, Game Genie input, save states and display filters.
resources.prerequisites: Your own SNES ROMs in Roms\ or paths configured in settings.xml. Keep Snes360.xex with the entire media folder, including Snes360.xzp, Snes360.ttf and compiled shaders.
resources.runtime: Xbox 360 able to run homebrew XEX files, including RGH/JTAG or a development kit. No exact motherboard or minimum system dashboard is published.
resources.temporary: No specific BadUpdate, ABadAvatar or Peer Pressure combination is certified by this release. The author says version 0.38 launch, UI navigation and gameplay still require hardware testing.
setup: The complete ZIP has Snes360.xex and media at its root. Extract all contents directly into the shown Snes360 folder.
Add your own ROMs to Roms or configure settings.xml, then launch Snes360.xex from Aurora, FSD or XeXMenu.
Preserve settings.xml, favorites.txt, saves and states when installing another version. Press both thumbsticks for the in-game menu.
resources.notes: Beta build. Achievement integration is removed. Supplied screenshots show an earlier interface version; they are publisher references, not hardware tests by this site.

image.credit: frankischilling · official ROM-browser screenshot; publisher says screenshot shows an earlier interface version

resources.title: Amiga360 Refresh 2026
resources.author: Vanni B. Monti-Condesnitt · Amiga360 / P-UAE contributors
resources.description: Controller-first Amiga emulator with machine profiles, multidisk swapping, savestates and Workbench hardfile support.
resources.prerequisites: Your own Kickstart 3.1 ROM at Kickstart\kick31.rom for A1200 startup, or Kickstart 1.3 at Kickstart\kick13.rom for A500. Put owned floppy images in Roms and hardfiles in Hardfiles. The release includes no Kickstart, Workbench, games, HDF collection or music.
resources.runtime: JTAG/RGH Xbox 360, explicitly required by the author. No particular motherboard or system-dashboard build is pinned.
resources.temporary: The publisher targets JTAG/RGH; no BadUpdate, ABadAvatar or Peer Pressure certification is provided.
setup: The 7z contains the runtime directly at its root. Extract all directories and A360RF26.xex together into the shown folder; keep media and the supplied Software helpers intact.
Supply your owned Kickstart and media in the exact folders above, then launch A360RF26.xex.
Preserve Config, SAVE, personal media and hardfiles between versions. If a Workbench hardfile misses its first boot, use Reset Amiga in the app before retrying.
resources.notes: The optional 115 MB Tools CD is not needed for the basic emulator and was not downloaded. The author reports hardware testing of this branch; this site did not run the build. Floppy formats include ADF, ADZ, DMS, FDI, compatible IPF, ZIP and M3U.

image.credit: Vanni B. Monti-Condesnitt · official GUI screenshot linked by the original-author README

resources.title: Ace Driver System 22 Collection
resources.author: wanszai
resources.description: Dedicated arcade emulator for Ace Driver Racing Evolution and Ace Driver Victory Lap, with offline solo play and display options.
resources.prerequisites: Supply your own acedrvrw.zip, victlapw.zip, namcoc71.zip and namcoc74.zip in roms\. Keep menu_assets.xpr beside default.xex. No ROM or game content is included.
resources.runtime: Native Xbox 360 XEX homebrew. The publisher does not pin a motherboard, dashboard minimum or a particular modification method; a compatible unsigned-code setup is required.
resources.temporary: The author does not certify a particular temporary exploit/payload combination or Peer Pressure. Do not infer it from another emulator.
setup: Extract the ZIP on your computer. Copy its whole AceDriverCollection folder into Emulators on your HDD or USB; avoid nesting another AceDriverCollection folder inside it.
Place your own four required ROM/driver ZIPs in the included roms folder. Keep them zipped.
Launch default.xex from an existing homebrew dashboard or file manager.
resources.notes: Version 1.0.1 fixes rebinding and a camera-switch acceleration issue. System Link/online play remains unfinished; force feedback is partial, and the documented difficulty control adds time rather than changing AI behavior.

image.credit: Xbox 360 console illustration · author supplies no project screenshot here

resources.title: DashLaunch GUI · temporary sessions
resources.author: 951261 · based on cOz DashLaunch
resources.description: Community DashLaunch settings editor adapted for BadUpdate and ABadAvatar sessions.
resources.prerequisites: An established BadUpdate or ABadAvatar runtime with launch.xex already loaded; XeUnshackle is the author’s example. Back up your launch.ini before editing. This app cannot load the module itself.
resources.runtime: BadUpdate / ABadAvatar Xbox 360 sessions, explicitly targeted by this community fork. BadUpdate itself requires dashboard 17559. No app-specific model list is supplied. This is separate from the normal persistent RGH/JTAG DashLaunch installer.
resources.temporary: Explicit temporary-session support. Re-run your exploit/runtime after reboot. Keep launch.xex loaded: using its unload/load controls can crash the console. Peer Pressure does not support this DashLaunch-plugin workflow.
setup: Copy the standalone original XEX into the shown applications folder; launch it only after your runtime has loaded launch.xex.
Edit the desired launch.ini settings in the GUI and explicitly save to the intended existing HDD/USB launch.ini. Keep a backup.
Return to your existing homebrew launcher. This tool is a beta editor and does not make a temporary exploit persistent.
resources.notes: The fork disables installer/uninstaller/patch-update buttons and removes most NAND-writing code, but FTP can still modify flash. Do not write to flash through FTP. The author gives no safety guarantee and still lists unverified NAND paths and unfinished fan controls. No downloaded build was run here.

image.credit: Xbox 360 console illustration · author supplies no project screenshot here

resources.title: Triangle · pinned runtime bundle
resources.author: JakobRangel
resources.description: Native package browser, download queue and file manager for independently operated homebrew sources.
resources.prerequisites: RGH/JTAG Xbox 360 and network access to your chosen compatible source server. Keep Triangle.xex, media, certs and sources.json together. Review the source URLs before downloading content.
resources.runtime: RGH/JTAG Xbox 360, explicitly targeted by the official project site. No exact dashboard build or motherboard list is published.
resources.temporary: The author does not certify BadUpdate, ABadAvatar or Peer Pressure for this alpha runtime.
setup: This is a local convenience ZIP assembled solely from the author’s ready runtime files at the pinned commit. Extract it on your PC; copy the contents of its Triangle-runtime-03cb4bc8e0e1 folder into the shown Triangle app directory.
Keep every original media/certs file and sources.json beside Triangle.xex, including the original secondary media/Triangle.xex.
Launch Triangle.xex using your existing homebrew dashboard, then review/add a trusted compatible source in Settings. The browser itself does not supply the content of third-party repositories.
resources.notes: Alpha snapshot, not an upstream ZIP release. The source repository contains ready binaries/resources rather than client source code. All 50 runtime originals were downloaded individually, their Git blob IDs checked, and their bytes retained unchanged in this bundle and staging manifest.

image.credit: JakobRangel · packaged Triangle dark splash artwork, not a UI screenshot

exclusions.reason: Source-only; no native XEX release asset in tree or releases. README describes return-to-XeLL, so this was not presented as a native XEX build.
